about: Locktenders takes its name from the keepers who work the locks of the Oswego Canal. Lock 1 itself sits across the street from the distillery in Phoenix, where cousins Brenden Backus, Stephen Dates and Kevin Dates opened Oswego County’s first post-Prohibition distillery in 2015. Gin came early in their story, added soon after their first vodka in 2017, and it helped the business along while the whiskey aged. Locktenders is the floral one of the distillery’s two gins; Drawbridge is the citrus-forward one.

The botanical bill starts with a classic London-style core of blue juniper, coriander, angelica root, orris root, cardamom and grains of paradise, then adds lavender and chamomile. The botanicals are macerated in Lock 1’s own spirit and distilled in small batches on stills the family built in their fabrication shop. It is bottled at 94 proof, strong enough to stand up in a martini or a gin and tonic.

In the glass Lock 1 describes a bright, juniper- and coriander-led opening, followed by lavender and chamomile once the first burst fades, and a softly sweet, faintly perfumed finish. The distillery suggests it for a gin and tonic or a lavender martini, where the floral side comes forward. Locktenders won a bronze medal at the New York State distilled spirits competition.
